ev.q: Cigarette smoking among U.S. adults declined from 20.9% in 2005 (45.1 million smokers) to 16.8% in 2014 (40.0 million)
Cigarette smoking was significantly lower in 2014 (16.8%) than in 2013 (17.8%) (p<0.05)
In 2014, prevalence was higher among males (18.8%) than females (14.8%)
the number of daily smokers decreased from 36.4 million (80.8% of all smokers) to 30.7 million (76.8%)
the mean number of cigarettes smoked per day declined from 16.7 in 2005 to 13.8 in 2014 (p<0.05 for trend)
Current cigarette smoking among U.S. adults declined from 20.9% (45.1 million persons) in 2005 to 16.8% (40.0 million) in 2014
Cigarette smoking was significantly lower in 2014 (16.8%) than in 2013 (17.8%) (p<0.05)

Logistic regression was used to analyze trends using annual NHIS data from 2005 through 2014.
To assess progress toward achieving the Healthy People 2020 objective of reducing the percentage of U.S. adults who smoke cigarettes to ≤12.0%

methods_quotes.q: Differences between groups were assessed using a Wald F -test, with statistical significance defined as p<0.05.
